value.a: SAME WORDS, DIFFERENT MEANING: 'this might break under load' in a build plan is a concern. 'This might break under load' in a closing summary is a caveat. The words are identical; the context is the signal.

POSITION IS THE CODE FLOOR'S ANSWER. Tool_use blocks are structural landmarks the code can see without understanding language. A concern before the last tool call is mid-work; a concern after all tool calls is closing-summary.

TRANSCRIPT_PATH IS THE STRUCTURAL SIGNAL. The stop-hook payload's last_assistant_message is text-only — no content blocks. The transcript JSONL at transcript_path carries the full content blocks with tool_use types, so tool positions are extracted from there, not from the payload text.

THE COORDINATE SYSTEM IS CUMULATIVE TEXT LENGTH. Tool_use blocks sit between text blocks; a tool's position is the sum of all preceding text block lengths. The concern's character offset in the concatenated text is compared to max(tool_positions) — before the last tool is mid-build, after is retrospective.

RETROSPECTIVE_CAVEAT IS SUPPRESSED, NOT DELETED. The classification rides the return dict; the hook's main() suppresses the receipt for retrospective_caveat but the red is still computed. A future LLM ceiling can re-read it.
